name: Box breathing
blurb: Breathe with a growing circle for one minute.
trains: Calm, focus and a slower heart rate
steps: Breathe in while the circle grows (4 seconds).
Hold gently (4 seconds).
Breathe out as it shrinks, then hold again.

bands.label: A start
bands.message: Even one slow breath tells your nervous system it can relax.

bands.label: Settling
bands.message: Nice. Your breathing is slowing down.

bands.label: Fully calm
bands.message: A full minute of steady breathing. Lovely work.

science: Slow, paced breathing at about 4–6 breaths a minute is widely used to calm the stress response. Box breathing is a simple version of it.
tip: Try this before a hard task or a meeting.

name: Memory pairs
blurb: Flip cards and find matching pairs.
steps: Tap a card to flip it.
Tap another card. If they match, they stay open.
Find all the pairs in as few moves as you can.

bands.label: Exploring
bands.message: You found them all. Next time, try to remember each card you flip.

bands.label: Excellent
bands.message: Very few wasted moves. Great spatial memory.

science: 8 moves is perfect (only possible with luck). Most relaxed players finish in roughly 14–22 moves. This is a Brain Games guide, not a clinical norm.
tip: Say what you see out loud in your head, “sun, top left”. Naming helps memory.

bands.label: Exploring
bands.message: You found them all. Next time, try to remember each card you flip.

bands.label: Excellent
bands.message: Very few wasted moves. Great spatial memory.

easy.science: Easy uses 6 pairs. 6 moves is perfect (only possible with luck). These bands are a Brain Games guide, not a clinical norm.

bands.label: Exploring
bands.message: You found them all. Ten pairs is a big board, so well done.

bands.label: Steady
bands.message: A calm, solid game on a big board.

bands.label: Good memory
bands.message: You’re holding a lot of positions in mind.

bands.label: Excellent
bands.message: Very few wasted moves on a hard board.

hard.science: Hard uses 10 pairs. 10 moves is perfect (only possible with luck). These bands are a Brain Games guide, not a clinical norm.

name: Odd colour out
blurb: Spot the one tile with a slightly different shade.
steps: A grid of same-coloured tiles appears.
One tile is a tiny bit lighter or darker. Tap it.
Grids get bigger and shades get closer. 60 seconds.

bands.label: Warming up
bands.message: Your eyes are tuning in. Relax your gaze instead of hunting tile by tile.

science: Colour-difference sensitivity varies with screen brightness and lighting, so compare yourself on the same device.
tip: Let your eyes soften and look at the whole grid. The odd tile often “pops”.

bands.label: Warming up
bands.message: Your eyes are tuning in. Relax your gaze instead of hunting tile by tile.

easy.science: Easy keeps the shade differences bigger for longer. Colour-difference sensitivity varies with screen brightness and lighting, and these bands are a Brain Games guide, not a clinical norm.

bands.label: Warming up
bands.message: Hard starts on a bigger grid with closer shades. Soften your gaze and let the odd tile pop.

bands.label: Good eye
bands.message: Nice colour sense on a tricky board.

hard.science: Hard starts on a bigger grid and the shades get close much faster. Colour-difference sensitivity varies with screen brightness and lighting, and these bands are a Brain Games guide, not a clinical norm.

name: Mental math
steps: A sum appears, like 23 + 18.
Type the answer. It moves on the moment you’re right.
Sums get harder as you go, up to the level you chose. 60 seconds.

bands.label: Warming up
bands.message: Your brain is switching gears. Scores usually jump after 2–3 tries.

bands.label: Steady
bands.message: About one answer every 6–10 seconds, including some harder sums. That’s a normal, healthy pace for someone not doing arithmetic daily.

bands.label: Sharp
bands.message: Quicker than most casual players. Your arithmetic is well practised.

bands.label: Quick
bands.message: Under 4 seconds per answer while sums get harder. Impressive.

science: There’s no standard clinical norm for this exact game, so these bands are a Brain Games guide based on seconds per answer. Speed comes from fact recall (knowing 7 × 8 instantly) plus holding numbers in working memory.

bands.label: Warming up
bands.message: Your brain is switching gears. Scores usually jump after 2–3 tries.

bands.label: Steady
bands.message: A calm, comfortable pace with small numbers. Keep going.

bands.label: Sharp
bands.message: Quick and accurate. Your everyday arithmetic is well practised.

easy.science: Easy keeps every sum to adding and subtracting small numbers, with no multiplying. These bands are a Brain Games guide based on seconds per answer, not a clinical norm.

bands.label: Warming up
bands.message: Big numbers and times tables from the start. Give it a few tries.

bands.label: Steady
bands.message: A solid pace on tough sums. Nicely done.

bands.label: Sharp
bands.message: Quicker than most players on big numbers. Your arithmetic is strong.

bands.label: Quick
bands.message: Under 5 seconds per answer on hard sums. Impressive.

bands.label: Lightning
bands.message: Calculator-level speed on the hard setting.

hard.science: Hard starts with big numbers and times tables from the first sum, so lower scores are normal. These bands are a Brain Games guide based on seconds per answer, not a clinical norm.

name: Serial sevens
blurb: Count down by 7 from a random number.
steps: You get a start number, like 143.
Type the number 7 less (136) and press Enter.
Keep going from your answer until the timer runs out.

bands.label: Warming up
bands.message: Holding a number while subtracting is genuinely hard. It gets easier fast.

science: Doctors use 5 serial sevens from 100 as a quick attention check, and healthy adults nearly always get all 5. These speed bands are a Brain Games guide.
tip: Subtract 10, then add 3. Many people find it easier.

bands.label: Warming up
bands.message: Holding a number while subtracting is genuinely hard. It gets easier fast.

easy.science: Easy gives 90 seconds. Doctors use 5 serial sevens from 100 as a quick attention check. These speed bands are a Brain Games guide.

bands.label: Warming up
bands.message: Forty seconds goes fast. Every step counts.

bands.label: Steady
bands.message: A calm, accurate pace under time pressure.

hard.science: Hard gives 40 seconds. Doctors use 5 serial sevens from 100 as a quick attention check. These speed bands are a Brain Games guide.

name: Reaction time
blurb: Tap the moment the box turns green.
steps: Wait while the box is calm.
Tap as soon as it turns green.
5 rounds. Tapping too early restarts the round.

bands.label: Sleepy day
bands.message: Usually tiredness or a slow device, not you.

bands.label: Relaxed
bands.message: Common when tired or winding down.

science: Online tests put the median human visual reaction at roughly 250–280 ms. Your screen and mouse add a little delay, so compare on the same device.
tip: Sleep and a short walk improve reaction time more than practice does.

name: Word sprint
blurb: As many words as you can from one letter.
steps: You get a letter, like S.
Type a word starting with it and press Enter.
Real words, 3+ letters, no repeats. Until the timer runs out.

bands.label: Very fluent
bands.message: You’re matching what people say out loud in clinical tests, while typing.

science: In the standard spoken letter-fluency test (F, A, S), adults average around 14–15 words per letter per minute. Typing is slower than speaking, so typed scores run lower.
tip: Think in themes: s-foods, s-animals, s-verbs.

easy.science: Easy gives 90 seconds. Spoken letter-fluency norms are per minute, so these bands are a Brain Games guide.

bands.label: Warming up
bands.message: Forty seconds is short. Every word counts.

bands.label: Very fluent
bands.message: Quick and steady under time pressure.

hard.science: Hard gives 40 seconds. Spoken letter-fluency norms are per minute, so these bands are a Brain Games guide.

name: Category challenge
blurb: Name things in a category before time runs out.
steps: You get a category, like Fruits.
Type an item and press Enter.
No repeats. Until the timer runs out.

bands.label: Warming up
bands.message: Some categories are much harder than others.

science: In spoken “name animals in 60 seconds” tests, younger adults usually say about 20. Typing slows things, so 13+ typed is very good.
tip: Use sub-groups: farm animals, then sea animals, then birds.

bands.label: Warming up
bands.message: Some categories are much harder than others.

easy.science: Easy gives 90 seconds. Spoken category-fluency norms are per minute, so these bands are a Brain Games guide.

bands.label: Warming up
bands.message: Forty seconds is short. Every item counts.

hard.science: Hard gives 40 seconds. Spoken category-fluency norms are per minute, so these bands are a Brain Games guide.

name: Backward spelling
blurb: See a word, then spell it in reverse.
steps: A word shows for a few seconds.
It disappears.
Type it backwards and press Enter. 8 rounds.

bands.label: Warming up
bands.message: Long words are tough. Picture the word written in front of you.

science: Spelling “WORLD” backwards is part of common memory screening. Holding and flipping letters uses the same working memory as backward digit span.
tip: Split long words: “ele-phant” → reverse each half, then swap.

bands.label: Warming up
bands.message: Short words are a gentle start. Picture the word written in front of you.

easy.science: Easy uses only the three shortest word groups (3 to 6 letters), so the bar is higher. These bands are a Brain Games guide, not a clinical norm.

bands.label: Warming up
bands.message: Long words are tough. Picture the word written in front of you.

bands.label: Steady
bands.message: Solid working memory on long words.

bands.label: Perfect
bands.message: Flawless, even on the longest words.

hard.science: Hard uses only the three longest word groups (6 to 8 letters), so the bar is lower. These bands are a Brain Games guide, not a clinical norm.

name: Digit span
blurb: Remember a growing string of numbers.
steps: Digits flash one at a time.
Type the whole string and press Enter.
Each success adds a digit. 2 misses ends.

bands.label: Warming up
bands.message: Distractions hit this test hard. Try a quiet moment.

science: The classic figure is 7 ± 2 digits. A large community sample averaged about 6.5 digits forward. With chunking practice, people have reached spans of 20+.
tip: Chunk like a phone number: 729-48 is easier than 7-2-9-4-8.

bands.label: Warming up
bands.message: Distractions hit this test hard. Try a quiet moment.

easy.science: Easy starts at 3 digits and shows each one more slowly, about 1.1 seconds apart. The bands sit a little higher than Medium. They are a Brain Games guide, not a clinical norm.

bands.label: Warming up
bands.message: Fast digits are tough. Try a quiet moment and go again.

bands.label: Typical
bands.message: A solid result at this quick pace.

bands.label: Strong
bands.message: Above average at a fast pace.

hard.science: Hard starts at 5 digits and shows each one faster, about 0.7 seconds apart, so a score is either 0 or 5 and up. The bands sit a little lower than Medium. They are a Brain Games guide, not a clinical norm.

name: Sequence memory
blurb: Repeat the pattern of lit squares.
steps: Watch squares light up one by one.
Tap them in the same order.
The pattern grows by one each level.

bands.label: Typical
bands.message: Visual spans usually sit 1–2 below number spans.

science: Visuospatial span is usually 1–2 items shorter than digit span. This game lets squares repeat, which is a bit harder than the clinical Corsi test.
tip: Trace the path as a shape: “L-shape, then corner.”

bands.label: Typical
bands.message: Visual spans usually sit 1–2 below number spans.

easy.science: Easy shows each square for 600 ms, one every 800 ms, so the pattern is slower to follow. These bands are a Brain Games guide, not a clinical norm.

bands.label: Warming up
bands.message: Fast patterns take a little practice. You’re getting there.

bands.label: Typical
bands.message: Keeping up with quick flashes is a real skill.

bands.label: Strong
bands.message: Very good spatial memory at speed.

hard.science: Hard shows each square for 250 ms, one every 450 ms, so the pattern flashes by quickly. These bands are a Brain Games guide, not a clinical norm.

name: N-back
blurb: Spot a letter that matches the one a few steps ago.
steps: Letters appear one by one.
If a letter matches the one N steps back, tap Match. N is 1, 2 or 3.
Otherwise do nothing. 24 letters.

demo.caption: On Medium: same as 2 back → tap

bands.label: Learning
bands.message: 2-back is honestly hard. Everyone starts here.

science: N-back is one of the most studied working-memory tasks in research. Healthy adults usually land around 75–90% on 2-back once they understand it.
tip: Whisper the last few letters to yourself on each step.

content.hint: Tap Match (or Space) when it’s the same as the letter {n} back

bands.label: Learning
bands.message: Everyone starts here. Watch for a letter that repeats.

easy.science: Easy is 1-back: tap when the letter matches the one just before it. These bands are a Brain Games guide.

bands.label: Learning
bands.message: 3-back is very hard. Everyone starts here.

bands.label: Getting it
bands.message: You’re keeping three letters in mind.

hard.science: Hard is 3-back: tap when the letter matches the one 3 steps ago. Research reports lower scores on 3-back than on 2-back. These bands are a Brain Games guide.

name: Stroop colours
blurb: Pick the ink colour, not the word.
steps: A colour word appears in a different ink.
Tap the INK colour, not the word.
Wrong taps cost a point. Until the timer runs out.

demo.scene: RED…but the ink is blue
demo.caption: Look at the ink

bands.label: Warming up
bands.message: Your reading brain is strong. It’s hard to ignore words.

science: The Stroop effect: reading is so automatic that naming ink colour is slower when the word conflicts. It’s a classic test of attention control.
tip: Blur your eyes slightly so the word is harder to read.

bands.label: Warming up
bands.message: Your reading brain is strong. It’s hard to ignore words.

easy.science: Easy gives 90 seconds. The Stroop effect is a classic test of attention control. These point bands are a Brain Games guide.

bands.label: Warming up
bands.message: Thirty seconds is short. Stay with the ink.

hard.science: Hard gives 30 seconds. The Stroop effect is a classic test of attention control. These point bands are a Brain Games guide.

name: Schulte table
blurb: Find the numbers in order in a scrambled grid.
steps: A grid of numbers appears.
Tap 1, then 2, then 3… up to the last number.
Keep your eyes near the centre.

bands.label: Warming up
bands.message: Take your time. Speed comes naturally.

science: Reference guides for adults put about 20 seconds at a moderate level and under 10 as excellent, usually on paper. Tapping on screen adds a little time.
tip: Look at the centre and let numbers find you in your side vision.

bands.label: Warming up
bands.message: Take your time. Speed comes naturally.

easy.science: Easy uses a 4×4 grid of 1 to 16. Published guides cover the 5×5 table only, so these bands are a Brain Games guide.

bands.label: Warming up
bands.message: A big grid. Take your time.

bands.label: Steady
bands.message: A relaxed pace on a big grid.

bands.label: Excellent
bands.message: Excellent scanning on a big grid.

hard.science: Hard uses a 6×6 grid of 1 to 36. Published guides cover the 5×5 table only, so these bands are a Brain Games guide.

name: Other hand day
blurb: Today’s tasks to do with your other hand.
steps: Read today’s 4 tasks.
Do them with your non-dominant hand during the day.
Tick them off, and try writing your name on the pad.

bands.label: Started
bands.message: Even trying is training. It feels clumsy because it’s new.

bands.label: Good effort
bands.message: Your brain is building new pathways.

bands.label: All done
bands.message: A full day of novelty. Brilliant.

science: Doing familiar things in an unfamiliar way adds novelty and attention to routine tasks. Expect it to feel awkward, that’s the point.
tip: Start with low-stakes tasks like scrolling your phone.

tasks: Write your name and today’s date on paper
Eat one meal with a spoon
Use the computer mouse for 10 minutes
Open every door you pass today
Draw a house, a tree and a sun
